fields.description:
## Context

DSO's LLM code review pipeline produces multi-cycle PRs that fail to converge. Empirical evidence (PR #65 escalated to user after 4 rounds with explicit "findings have not converged"; PR #62 oscillated 8->8->6 across 3 rounds; ~10-12 of ~50 post-feature PRs took >2 cycles; admin-merge-with-failure on #45 and #65) traces to four interlocking architectural causes: reviewers stateless across cycles, broken CI/local prompt parity, mid-resolution tier ratcheting that introduces fresh-perspective findings, and lack of a structured terminator for sustained disagreement. This epic ships statefulness, parity, arbitration, and tier-decoupling so reframing-oscillation and local-vs-CI divergence stop driving cycle counts.

## User Experience Change

After this ships, a developer running `/dso:review` on a PR that had findings in cycle N will see each cycle-N+1 finding tagged NEW_INTRODUCED, NEW_PRE_EXISTING, RESUSTAIN_OF, or REFRAME_OF — making it immediately visible whether the reviewer is introducing a new concern or re-raising a prior one. CI llm-review will load the same agent prompt files as local `/dso:review`, so findings that pass locally will not silently fail in CI. When a previously defended finding is re-raised, an opus arbiter resolves it within the same review run (sustain, accept defense, or downgrade severity) instead of escalating to the user after MAX_ATTEMPTS. Current state: P90 cycle_count is well above 2 (~10-12 of every ~50 PRs require >2 cycles); target post-ship: P90 cycle_count <= 2.

## Success Criteria

1. **Stateful re-review with two-call reviewer architecture, orchestrator-side proximity-overlap verification, and severity-history telemetry.** Cycle-N+1 reviewers run as **two structurally independent litellm/Agent calls** rather than a single prompt with a content-marker gate (the gate is not enforceable through transformer attention). **Call 1 (diff-only)**: reviewer receives the diff plus a structured `prior_findings_index` (finding IDs + cited_lines + dimension only — NO defense_text). Returns initial findings JSON without `relation` fields. **Call 2 (relation assignment)**: reviewer receives Call 1's output, the full `prior_findings.json` (including dimension and severity), and `defenses[]`. Returns the same findings annotated with `relation` (NEW_INTRODUCED, NEW_PRE_EXISTING, RESUSTAIN_OF, REFRAME_OF), optional `prior_finding_id`, and optional `escape_rationale` (free-text, max 512 chars; structured enum deferred to implementation-plan). First-cycle reviews remain a single call (no `prior_findings_index`, no Call 2). Schema and rules live in `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-findings-schema.md` (created in Phase 2). Auto-downgrade rule: NEW_PRE_EXISTING auto-downgrades to `minor` UNLESS the referenced `prior_finding_id` was previously rated `important` or `critical` (re-elevation of previously-minor findings prohibited without explicit `ESCALATE_REVIEW`). NEW_INTRODUCED on lines in cycle-N fix delta is unrestricted. **Orchestrator-side proximity-overlap verification (RESUSTAIN escape-hatch guard)**: after Call 2 returns, the orchestrator computes proximity overlap between each new finding's `cited_lines` and every entry in `prior_findings.json` — overlap means same file AND line ranges intersect OR are within ±5 lines of each other. If proximity overlap exists and the reviewer declared `NEW_INTRODUCED` without `escape_rationale`, the orchestrator rejects the relation and re-dispatches Call 2 with the message "Finding cited_lines are within ±5 lines of prior finding `<id>` in the same file; re-classify as RESUSTAIN_OF, REFRAME_OF, or provide explicit escape_rationale that names a substantive distinction beyond line numbers." **Severity-history telemetry**: each finding records its severity-history across cycles in the DefenseStore. The metric `phantom_escalation_rate` (cycle-1 important findings never RESUSTAIN_OF'd in subsequent cycles) is named in the SC6 monitoring plan as a leading indicator of severity-inflation drift; threshold tuning deferred to first 30-day telemetry. **Call 2 completeness check**: after Call 2 returns, the orchestrator asserts that every finding ID present in Call 1's output is present in Call 2's annotated output (modulo any IDs proximity-overlap-rejected between calls). Missing IDs trigger a single Call 2 re-dispatch with the message "Finding `<id>` was present in Call 1 but absent from your response; include it with an appropriate relation." Persistently missing findings (still absent after re-dispatch) are carried forward with `relation: NEW_INTRODUCED` as a safe default and surfaced in `review-stats.sh` under `call2_finding_drop_rate` (a second named telemetry metric in SC6). **`escape_rationale` structural validation**: when supplied, the rationale must reference at least one token or cited-line pattern present in the new finding's diff context but NOT in (a) the prior finding's `cited_lines` content and NOT in (b) the ±5-line proximity overlap region. The orchestrator verifies syntactically (token presence/absence in source ranges) — no LLM call required. Rationales that fail this structural check are rejected and the finding is treated as if no `escape_rationale` were provided (re-dispatch with re-classify instruction). **Prior-salience suppression telemetry**: a third named metric, `prior_region_resustain_skew`, tracks the ratio of RESUSTAIN_OF to NEW_INTRODUCED findings on code regions flagged in prior cycles. Anomalous skew (heavily RESUSTAIN-weighted with low NEW_INTRODUCED density) signals attention-suppression in Call 1 from the `prior_findings_index` and is monitored alongside `phantom_escalation_rate`.

2. **Single source of truth for review prompts (CI parity, scoped to prompt content) with documented fidelity tolerance.** `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py`'s hardcoded 5-line `_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is removed. CI loads the same `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-*.md` agent files used by `/dso:review` and injects them as the `litellm.completion()` system prompt. CI uses `review-complexity-classifier.sh` (with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` bootstrap added to ci.yml — verified by a smoke-test CI step before classifier.py removal), the same overlay dispatch logic (parallel litellm calls per overlay flag), the same schema validation, and the same severity rubric and NOT-flag rules. **Explicit scope decision**: Phase 1 parity is "same prompts via litellm" — NOT "same Agent-tool dispatch architecture." Deep-tier opus arch synthesis in CI is approximated by a single opus litellm call with `deep-arch.md` as system prompt operating on merged sonnet specialist outputs (themselves 3 parallel litellm calls). Documented in `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ci-vs-local-parity-scope.md`. **Fidelity tolerance acceptance criterion**: the CI deep-tier verdict must agree with the local deep-tier verdict on each fixture PR (SC6) within one severity band on every finding (e.g., local `critical` may not become CI `minor`; one-band drift is acceptable). If fixture divergence exceeds tolerance, Phase 1 is rolled back until the approximation is improved. **Two-call reviewer architecture (SC1) is implemented identically in CI**: cycle-N+1 reviews dispatch two litellm calls (Call 1 diff-only, Call 2 with prior_findings + defenses). **Orchestrator-side overlap verification runs in CI** with a single re-dispatch cap (one re-dispatch per cycle, not per finding); if a second misclassification is detected after re-dispatch, the orchestrator emits `ESCALATE_REVIEW: relation_misclassification_unresolved` and proceeds without the rejected finding rather than continuing to retry. CI delta from local: (a) existing `REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci` injection, (b) worktree-vs-CI artifact path resolution, (c) Agent-tool-vs-litellm dispatch (documented), (d) re-dispatch cap (single retry vs unbounded local).

3. **DefenseStore with split backends, shared loader/writer, ticket-binding integrity, and explicit ordering contract.** A shared `DefenseStore` interface has two backends: `TrackerDefenseStore` (writes to ticket comments — used by `/dso:review`) and `GitHubPRDefenseStore` (writes to PR comments — used by CI). Both serialize the same record shape: `prior_finding_id`, `cited_lines_fingerprint`, `defense_text` (max 4096 chars), `defender`, `cycle_number`, `timestamp`, `severity_history[]` (per-cycle severity record for SC1 telemetry), optional `arbiter_ruling` (full text only in TrackerDefenseStore; GitHubPRDefenseStore stores 1-2 sentence summary with link). Schema and storage at `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md`. **Ticket-binding integrity**: local review without a session-bound ticket fails with exit code 1 and stderr containing the literal string `ticket-binding required` (test: `tests/review/test-defense-store-ticket-binding.sh`). Multi-bound sessions write to the most-recently-active story (or epic if no story); the bound ticket ID is written into each defense record. **`cited_lines_fingerprint` is computed by the orchestrator**: SHA-256 of the concatenation of `<path>:<line_number>:<whitespace-collapsed-line-content>` for each cited line; whitespace-only changes preserve, semantic edits void. **Mirror-at-PR-open ordering contract**: a `mirror-defenses-to-pr` workflow step runs as a `needs:` dependency before `llm-review` in ci.yml; idempotently posts all tracker defenses for the PR's tickets. Soft fallback: `GitHubPRDefenseStore.load()` falls through to `TrackerDefenseStore` if the mirror has not run. **Fork-PR fallback**: `GitHubPRDefenseStore.write()` detects head_repo != base_repo and downgrades to no-op + logged warning; CI on fork PRs reads from `TrackerDefenseStore` only. **Bidirectional load on local**: `/dso:review` reads from TrackerDefenseStore by default but ALSO reads from GitHubPRDefenseStore when run against a branch with an open PR. **`load_for_region(region_files)` semantics**: returns the same records as `load()` filtered to those with any `cited_lines` path intersecting `region_files`; the no-op default returns all records unfiltered. Both backends implement identically; activates if/when f61f-7e0a Strategy E ships.

4. **Opus arbiter with trinary authority, structured severity_rebuttal, and durable fingerprint binding.** When a finding ID `X` is defended in cycle N (defense recorded in store) and re-raised in cycle N+1 (relation: RESUSTAIN_OF X), the orchestrator dispatches a single opus arbiter (new agent file: `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-arbiter.md`). Inputs: the finding, the defense, the cited diff hunks, the `reviewer-base.md` severity rubric and NOT-flag rules. Trinary output: `SUSTAIN_AT_SEVERITY` (uphold reviewer), `ACCEPT_DEFENSE` (dismiss), `DOWNGRADE_TO_<severity>` (real concern, lower severity). **Anti-compromise discipline via structured rebuttal**: every `DOWNGRADE_TO` output MUST include a `severity_rebuttal` field with three subfields: (a) `reviewer_claimed_severity` (verbatim from the reviewer's finding), (b) `reviewer_severity_evidence` (verbatim quote from the reviewer's finding text supporting the severity), (c) `named_rebuttal` (concrete, cited-lines-backed argument why that specific evidence does not support the claimed severity). The orchestrator's schema validator rejects DOWNGRADE_TO outputs whose `named_rebuttal` is generic; rejected DOWNGRADE_TO is reclassified as ACCEPT_DEFENSE. **Two-layer rejection**: (a) **structural check** (primary, model-output-invariant) — `named_rebuttal` MUST cite at least one `<file>:<line>` reference that is NOT present in `reviewer_severity_evidence`. A rebuttal introducing no new cited evidence is structurally generic regardless of token content. (b) **token-overlap heuristic** (secondary) — token-overlap with `reviewer_severity_evidence` below threshold OR matches generic-template patterns. The structural check is the primary rejection mechanism (no threshold tuning required); the heuristic is a defense-in-depth secondary guard. The arbiter prompt also includes the explicit instruction: "DOWNGRADE_TO is NOT a compromise mechanism. It is for cases where the reviewer's severity is specifically too high but the underlying concern is real. If you find yourself selecting DOWNGRADE_TO because you are uncertain between SUSTAIN and ACCEPT, you MUST select ACCEPT_DEFENSE instead." Decision recorded as a defense record with `arbiter: true` and `cited_lines_fingerprint` snapshotted. **Durable binding scoped to fingerprint**: subsequent cycles must not re-raise this ID against this code state. If cited lines change, NEW_INTRODUCED authority applies (with proximity-overlap rationale per SC1) and produces a fresh finding with a fresh ID. Whitespace-only changes preserve binding; semantic edits release it.

5. **Tier upgrade decoupled from cycle-attempt count, including HUGE workflow and short-circuit oscillation detection.** Tier upgrades occur exclusively on explicit `ESCALATE_REVIEW` from the resolution sub-agent. The `PASS_NUM>=2` light->standard ratchet (anchor: conditional block beginning `if [ "${REVIEW_PASS_NUM}" -ge 2 ]` near the tier-escalation section in REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md) and the MAX_ATTEMPTS->deep upgrade (anchor: post-loop block following `MAX_ATTEMPTS exceeded`) are removed. **REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md FALLBACK** is reviewed for ratchet patterns and updated to match the ESCALATE_REVIEW-only model, or divergence is documented. `review.max_resolution_attempts` is retained as a backstop. **Short-circuit oscillation detection**: if the orchestrator observes the same file+region (±5 lines) appearing in two consecutive NEW_INTRODUCED findings without `escape_rationale`, it emits `ESCALATE_REVIEW: oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement` immediately (after cycle 2, not after MAX_ATTEMPTS). This complements SC1's per-cycle proximity-overlap verification and short-circuits the failure mode where a reviewer cites non-overlapping adjacent lines to bypass arbitration. Test: regression test asserts (a) tier stays at initial value across 2+ resolution cycles with no ESCALATE_REVIEW signal; (b) ast-grep/grep scan confirms ratchet logic absent from REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md; (c) two-cycle proximity-repeat triggers immediate oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement escalation.

6. **Migration via best-effort file-path binding, fixture-based validation, and forward telemetry.** A migration script scans the repo for `# REVIEW-DEFENSE:` source comments (currently 154 instances), extracts each into a defense record bound to its file's primary owning ticket (most-recent epic story touching that file path); ambiguous cases marked `ticket: UNBOUND` and surfaced in the audit log. Records are written to `TrackerDefenseStore` (bound) or to a top-level "Legacy REVIEW-DEFENSE corpus" ticket (UNBOUND). Inline comments are deleted in a single atomic commit. The reviewer-base.md REVIEW-DEFENSE Evaluation section (anchor: section heading `## REVIEW-DEFENSE Evaluation` or equivalent) and review-fix-dispatch.md inline-comment guidance are removed in the same commit. **The pre-commit citation-check hook from b6e9-6f1d G5-M1 is also removed in this commit** (it has no remaining target post-cutover). Cutover protocol: communicate cutover date; pre-cutover both old (inline) and new (DefenseStore) mechanisms are honored; post-cutover only DefenseStore is read; CLAUDE.md updated atomically. **Validation (fixture-based)**: PR #65 and PR #62 diffs checked into `tests/fixtures/review-convergence/<pr-id>.diff` along with prior-cycle findings JSON; harness asserts (a) RESUSTAIN_OF X with proximity overlap triggers exactly one arbiter dispatch on the same finding ID, (b) NEW_INTRODUCED on overlapping/proximate lines without escape_rationale is rejected and re-dispatched, (c) NEW_PRE_EXISTING auto-downgrades unless prior was important+, (d) DOWNGRADE_TO without valid named_rebuttal is reclassified as ACCEPT_DEFENSE. **Easy-path regression check**: 5 SHA-pinned single-cycle PRs from the last 90 days as fixtures; new pipeline produces equivalent findings (modulo new relation fields) and remains single-cycle. **Forward telemetry**: for 30 days post-ship, `review-stats.sh` reports four named metrics — `p90_cycle_count` (target <=2), `phantom_escalation_rate` (cycle-1 importants never RESUSTAIN_OF'd; threshold tuning deferred to first 30-day data), `call2_finding_drop_rate` (Call 2 re-dispatch and carry-forward rate per SC1), and `prior_region_resustain_skew` (RESUSTAIN_OF vs NEW_INTRODUCED density on prior-flagged regions; suppression indicator per SC1). **Response playbook**: alert owner is the review-pipeline maintainer. Provisional response — when `phantom_escalation_rate` exceeds threshold for two consecutive 7-day windows, open a P2 bug against the cycle-1 severity rubric and link the telemetry report. Same playbook applies to `prior_region_resustain_skew` anomalies (P2 bug against the two-call architecture / prior_findings_index design). Threshold values themselves are deferred to first 30-day data; response protocol is specified now to avoid spec-revision lag when telemetry arrives.

## Scenario Analysis

Surviving red-team scenarios after blue-team filter (5 of 14):

- **Inverse RESUSTAIN_OF gaming** (`high`, `escape_hatch`): Reviewer mis-labels a genuinely new finding as RESUSTAIN_OF to weaponize the arbiter and bypass NEW_PRE_EXISTING auto-downgrade. SC1 proximity-overlap guards declaring NEW_INTRODUCED on nearby lines but does not guard the inverse mis-classification. Mitigation deferred to implementation-plan: orchestrator-side check that RESUSTAIN_OF ID exists in `prior_findings.json` (already required by schema) plus a confidence check that the prior finding's cited_lines are within proximity of the new finding's; if not, reject as malformed RESUSTAIN_OF.
- **Multi-bound session "most-recently-active" tiebreak undefined** (`high`, `integrity`): SC3 says "writes to the most-recently-active story (or epic if no story)" without defining the recency function (last-touched? last-transitioned? last-commented?) or the same-second tiebreak. Mitigation in implementation-plan: define recency as last `ticket transition` or last `ticket comment` timestamp (whichever is later); same-timestamp tiebreak by lexicographic ticket-ID.
- **Line-number drift from positional rebases voids fingerprint without semantic change** (`high`, `integrity`): The fingerprint includes `line_number`, so inserting/deleting unrelated lines above a defended region voids the binding. Whitespace-collapse in content protects against formatting; line drift is unguarded. Accepted constraint with a follow-on: if telemetry shows excessive arbiter-binding releases on regions whose content didn't change, follow-up bug to switch fingerprint to AST-relative or content-hash-only.
- **MAX_ATTEMPTS exhaustion outside the proximity short-circuit window** (`high`, `escape_hatch`): A reviewer that consistently cites genuinely non-overlapping regions (outside ±5 lines) without same-file repetition can exhaust `review.max_resolution_attempts` without triggering oscillation detection or arbiter dispatch. SC5 names the safety-net signal `ESCALATE_REVIEW: oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement` but specifies it primarily for the proximity-repeat case. Mitigation in implementation-plan: extend the same `ESCALATE_REVIEW` to fire on ANY MAX_ATTEMPTS exhaustion without an arbiter dispatch in the cycle history (independent of proximity), so this exit path is reachable for the non-proximity case.
- **GitHub PR comment rate limits on bulk mirror/append** (`medium`, `ci`): Mirror-at-PR-open posts all tracker defenses for the PR's tickets; large PRs with many cycles can hit GitHub's secondary rate limits. SC3 has no retry/backoff. Mitigation in implementation-plan: GitHubPRDefenseStore implements exponential backoff on 429/secondary-rate-limit responses; mirror batches comments with an inter-batch delay; on persistent failure, the soft fallback to TrackerDefenseStore.load() activates so reviewers continue to see defenses.

All 5 surviving scenarios have concrete mitigation paths that fit within the existing 3-phase implementation structure; no scenario warrants a structural redesign of the epic.

## Approach

**Sequential implementation in three phases.** Each phase is shippable independently with its own PR(s) under the per-story PR size budget.

**Phase 1 — CI parity scoped to prompt content (SC2).** Rewrite `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` to load `code-reviewer-*.md` files. Bootstrap `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in ci.yml; smoke-test classifier.sh in CI before classifier.py removal. Document dispatch-architecture delta and fidelity tolerance in parity-scope contract. Two-call reviewer architecture (SC1) is wired through dispatch.py at the same time so it activates uniformly in Phase 2. Layers on top of 2fa0-a2d9 (in-flight context-augmentation loop, brainstorm-complete, status: open); 2fa0 ships first.

**Phase 2 — Statefulness, arbitration, tier-decoupling (SC1, SC3-tracker, SC4, SC5).** Add relation taxonomy and contracts. Implement `DefenseStore` interface + `TrackerDefenseStore` backend + orchestrator-side proximity-overlap verification + escape-rationale gate + severity-history telemetry. Update reviewer dispatch to two-call architecture (Call 1 diff-only, Call 2 relation-assignment). Add `code-reviewer-arbiter.md` with structured `severity_rebuttal` schema and orchestrator schema validator. Update REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md to remove cycle-count tier ratchets; add short-circuit oscillation detection. **Granularity at implementation-plan**: SC3-tracker is split into at least 2 stories (interface + TrackerBackend; fingerprint computation + telemetry); SC4 arbiter is its own story; SC1 orchestrator verification is its own story. Local stays on tracker backend.

**Phase 3 — PR backend, mirror, migration (SC3-PR, SC6).** Implement `GitHubPRDefenseStore` with fork-PR fallback. Implement mirror-at-PR-open workflow step + soft fallback. Run the one-shot migration commit (also removes b6e9-6f1d G5-M1 pre-commit hook). Validate against fixtures. Begin 30-day forward telemetry.

## Dependencies

- **Supersedes b6e9-6f1d** ("Reviewer override discipline: defense citations, downgrade quorum, isolation-ok registry"). Both target REVIEW-DEFENSE self-attestation; this epic's structured DefenseStore + arbiter is the more comprehensive replacement. b6e9-6f1d's downgrade-quorum and isolation-ok-registry concepts are subsumed by orchestrator-side proximity-overlap verification (SC1) and arbiter binding (SC4); G5-M1 pre-commit citation hook is removed in SC6 migration commit. On approval, b6e9-6f1d is closed as superseded with a comment linking here. **Formal dep link to be added post-approval.**
- **Depends on 2fa0-a2d9** ("CI context-augmentation loop, prompt caching, turn-budget exhaustion") — `brainstorm:complete`, status: open. Phase 1 parity layers on top of 2fa0-a2d9's multi-turn dispatch.py; 2fa0 ships first. **Formal `depends_on` link to be added post-approval.**
- **Coordinates with 5018-64ce** ("Evaluate and resolve current TODO/FIXME/HACK and REVIEW-DEFENSE comments"). SC6 migration is the authoritative REVIEW-DEFENSE removal path; idempotent against partial removal.
- **Layers on closed epic 6da2-4cff** (severity calibration, NOT-flag, REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci, cited_lines). New schema fields coexist in distinct sections.
- **Coordinates with f61f-7e0a** (Per-Story PR Review Structure). DefenseStore interface includes `load_for_region(region_files)` from day 1 (no-op default); region scoping activates if Strategy E ships.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- **reviewer-base.md and code-reviewer-*.md.** Layers on 6da2-4cff. New schema sections (relation taxonomy, two-call architecture, defense-loader guidance) coexist without colliding with severity/NOT-flag headings. Gate: build-review-agents.sh produces all 10 agents with all required sections after merge.
- **dso_ci_review/dispatch.py.** Hard ordering with 2fa0-a2d9: 2fa0 ships first; Phase 1 layers parity. Gate: dispatch.py post-Phase-1 must pass 2fa0-a2d9's acceptance tests.
- **review-fix-dispatch.md and resolution loop.** Resolution sub-agent consumes DefenseStore via Bash CLI (NOT nested Task dispatch — per CLAUDE.md rule 17). Gate: Step 3 "Defend findings" updated atomically with Phase 2.
- **oscillation-check skill.** SC1 proximity-overlap and SC5 short-circuit subsume the literal-diff-reversal check. Gate: assess deprecation in implementation plan; until decided, both run.
- **REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md.** SC5 explicitly covers HUGE workflow tier-ratchet review.
- **ci.yml workflow.** New `mirror-defenses-to-pr` step + CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT bootstrap are additive.

## Open Questions for Implementation Plan

- Whether to entirely withhold `prior_findings_index` from Call 1 (sacrificing relation-matching quality for full prior-salience independence) or retain the v5 design with `prior_region_resustain_skew` telemetry as the suppression-detection mechanism. Implementation plan reviews telemetry trade-off.
- Format of `escape_rationale` (default free-text 512 chars; structured enum may follow telemetry).
- Threshold tuning for `phantom_escalation_rate` (deferred to first 30-day telemetry).
- Heuristic threshold for arbiter `named_rebuttal` token-overlap rejection (deferred to first arbiter telemetry).
- Whether to gate non-arbiter resolution sub-agent dispatches on DefenseStore reads, or treat reads as best-effort.
- Storage location for the "Legacy REVIEW-DEFENSE corpus" ticket (new dedicated meta-ticket vs append to existing).

- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: not triggered (prior research from upstream root-cause analysis already informed the design)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered

- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: triggered — cycles: 1, gap: CI Agent-tool unavailability + fork-PR token scope + mirror ordering race + migration ticket-binding hit rate
